scope: Review current ACadSharp release changes for large-document writer scalability, DXF table-count boundaries, missing-layer recovery, and partial-read evidence; refine existing plan owners without expanding routine validation cost.

method.kind: Current ACadSharp releases and merged PR discussions, LibreDWG and ezdxf documentation, Autodesk table contract, and local PAR-120/7BQ/source/test-owner cross-check
method.evidenceRule: Peer measurements, release notes, PR reports and issue status are source-level design and test-selection evidence only. No peer behavior is inferred to be a libdxfrw defect or a format-wide support claim.

evidence.observed: Merged PR #1168 describes two full entity scans per BlockRecord in writeBlockHeader, producing O(blocks × entities) work, and replaces them with one lazily built/reused lookup. The PR reports net9 measurements at source master 219e5fc: 20,000 blocks/inserts fell from 29.47s to 1.56s. This is a contributor-reported measurement, not independently reproduced here.
doesNotEstablish: a corresponding complexity defect in libdxfrw
the same timing on other runtimes, hardware, or document mixes
that a broad benchmark or performance gate should run for every implementation slice
evidence.planUse: Before changing a scale-sensitive traversal, inspect its complexity and ownership keys. Where repeated scans are actually present, build a bounded, reusable index once per phase and retain deterministic ordering. Use one small generated scale smoke or benchmark only after a relevant optimization composes; keep it outside the routine per-slice fast loop.

evidence.topic: DXF symbol-table group-70 counts beyond signed 16-bit range
evidence.observed: Merged ACadSharp #1192 reports a production drawing with over 40,000 BLOCK_RECORD entries that failed serialization when the group-70 value was checked into Int16. The contributor reports AutoCAD 2027 accepted a table header group-70 value of zero while consuming the following entries; a wrapped negative value also reportedly opened. The PR's prose contains inconsistent record totals (40,843 versus 41,043), so the exact fixture denominator is not suitable as a benchmark. Current local 7BQ intentionally tests exact capacities through 32767 and rejects 32768.
doesNotEstablish: a normative rule that zero is always the correct overflow encoding
that every CAD reader ignores group 70 or counts entries the same way
that an unexecuted AutoCAD report proves current libdxfrw output acceptance
evidence.planUse: Keep the local exact-count <=32767 contract and current fail-closed overflow behavior. Add a separately gated PAR-120 follow-up: generated scratch output just above the boundary, a candidate zero/unknown count header while retaining every row, strict local readback with full row and following-table sentinels, then one exact-version AutoCAD/independent-reader check if available. Do not add the reported production drawing or spend this composed test in each slice.

evidence.topic: DXF input with a named but undefined layer
evidence.observed: Merged ACadSharp #1245 says its DXF builder previously warned and silently placed entities whose group-8 layer name was absent from the LAYER table on layer 0. The change creates one shared layer with default properties and retains the name; its author says this matches AutoCAD's behavior. The PR identifies this as an invalid-file repair policy and notes that only unresolved name-based references are affected.
doesNotEstablish: that the malformed source is valid under the DXF contract
that synthesizing a default layer is appropriate for libdxfrw or LibreCAD consumers
that a successful ordinary load preserves exact source graph/table semantics
evidence.planUse: Add a generated hostile compatibility control under existing PAR-20/graph admission owners only if current tests lack it: preserve the literal entity layer name, report unresolved table identity, and ensure export either explicitly synthesizes a documented default layer or fails before publication rather than silently changing the entity to layer 0. Keep any repair mode opt-in and preserve ordinary LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 behavior until a local reproducer and consumer requirement exist.

evidence.topic: Partial section-read status and comparator refresh
evidence.observed: ACadSharp issue #339, requesting section-by-section DXF reads for problematic or unsupported-version files, is closed and cross-links #342. The available issue page confirms status but the linked PR details were not available in this review; no claim is made about its exact released API or behavior. ACadSharp's current release page identifies v3.8.0 as latest on the reviewed snapshot.
doesNotEstablish: that partial reads are full-document validation or lossless acceptance
that #342's precise implementation is present in a selected runtime without checking its release/source
that ACadSharp v3.8.0 was executed for this review
evidence.planUse: Refresh any future peer manifest to v3.8.0 or a pinned SHA and identify which API was used. Report section extraction separately from whole-document validity, ownership closure, and semantic acceptance; retain the existing partial-versus-full outcome fields.

fastPerSliceChecks: lc3_compat_check if public API or adapter compatibility changes
oneTimeComposedChecks: one generated >32767 table-row stress case with actual-row and following-table sentinels
one pinned strict-reader/native acceptance for any candidate overflow header policy
one scale smoke only for a source-confirmed repeated-scan hotspot
one generated unresolved-layer identity control if current coverage is absent
implementationReadiness.fixturePolicy: Do not download or commit the large ACadSharp production drawing. Generate any stress input in memory or in a temporary directory and remove it after the run.
implementationReadiness.nonPromotion: No support claim or external J disposition changes. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293 and J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL.
